equity_bridge.note: 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet; pro-rata JV EBITDAre ~$61M/yr is excluded from the consolidated EBITDA the flows use, so the asset is added back here (matching-asset rule). Book is conservative against ~12x the pro-rata EBITDA less pro-rata debt.

equity_bridge.note: 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet, carried at redemption (fair) value. Flows are consolidated; the units are exchangeable into common, so their claim is deducted here instead of being added to the share count.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: owner_fcf_3yr_cagr (FY2022-FY2025, 3.1%) cross-checked against the pre-COVID-to-now revenue CAGR (FY2019-FY2025, 1.9%) and the RevPAR-led run-rate; both bracket ~2.5-3.5% nominal for a no-acquisition portfolio.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 5-year CAGRs are meaningless: FY2020 is the COVID trough (revenue $1,620M, EBITDA negative, EPS -1.04), so the 30.4% 5-yr revenue CAGR is recovery arithmetic, and EPS 5-yr is undefined. Equity CAGR (~0%) is also not a growth signal for a REIT that distributes >90% of taxable income and buys back stock; it is not used. Owner-FCF series (EBITDA - SBC - cash tax - total capex): FY2019 699, FY2022 812, FY2023 776, FY2024 738, FY2025 889.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (3.1%) is below the reported-EBITDA 3-yr CAGR (4.7%) because total capex rose from $621M (FY2022) to $724M (FY2025) with the Hyatt/Marriott transformational programs and hurricane reconstruction; the capex burden, not SBC (0.4% of revenue), is what separates reported from owner cash flow at Host.

scenario_narratives.base: Host stays a rate-led, no-acquisition luxury/upper-upscale portfolio. FY2026 lands at the raised guidance ($6.14B revenue, 27.3% EBITDA margin) but that margin includes World Cup, Maui base-effect and condo/BI one-offs, so FY2027 gives back ~20bps and margins then hold at ~27%, where Host has sat in every normal year since FY2016. Revenue grows ~3% on RevPAR plus renovation ramp, fading to 2.5%. All capex (R&R plus the brand-mandated Hyatt/Marriott ROI programs, ~10% of revenue) is charged; cash taxes stay at the TRS level because REIT status is permanent. Unlevered owner FCF runs ~$1.0B (62% of EBITDA), discounted at a 9% USD WACC with 2.5% terminal growth. The ~$1.3B of pro-forma cash from the Four Seasons sale is netted against debt; how management deploys it (buybacks, acquisitions, another special) is value-neutral here.
scenario_narratives.bull: The luxury travel cycle extends. Affluent leisure and group demand keep rate growing 4-5% against a luxury pipeline that is effectively closed, the renovated Hyatt and Marriott assets earn their RevPAR premiums, Maui completes its recovery, and margins expand ~120bps to 28.5% as rate outruns wage inflation. Capex normalises toward 9% of revenue once the transformational programs finish. The stock re-rates toward the ~12-13x EV/EBITDA that private buyers paid Host for its own dispositions.
scenario_narratives.bear: The expansion ends in 2027. A consumer or corporate-travel slowdown hits the most cyclical REIT subsector: revenue falls 8% then 4%, and because Host bears the full hotel P&L (no fixed leases) the EBITDA margin compresses to 22% - about half the FY2007-09 damage. Brand standards keep capex from being cut far. Recovery from 2029 returns margins to 26%, 100bps below today, as labour, property-tax and coastal insurance costs reset higher; climate event risk in Maui and Florida remains live. Net debt of $3.8B at 4.7-year maturity means no solvency risk, but distributions and buybacks pause.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Host is valued as what it is: an owner of ~75 luxury and upper-upscale hotels whose cash flow is hotel EBITDA less the heavy, non-optional renovation capex those flags demand. The DCF is unlevered at a 9% USD WACC with every dollar of capex charged and REIT-level (near-zero) cash tax held permanently; net debt is pro forma for the July 2026 special dividend, JV stakes are added at book and OP units deducted. AFFO capitalisation was considered and rejected because Host's Adjusted FFO is pre-capex; a FAD-at-cost-of-equity cross-check lands within a dollar of the base case. The value is dominated by the terminal multiple, so the honest readings are the implied EV/EBITDA and the required-return table rather than the point estimate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cyclicality: the bear case models a 2027-28 downturn at half the FY2007-09 severity; a full repeat (revenue -21%, margin 18%) is outside the bear path
Capex assumption: charging ROI capex with only ~3% revenue growth may understate the return on the Hyatt/Marriott programs (upside) or, if brand standards escalate, overstate free cash (downside)
Terminal multiple: the base case implies ~10x EV/EBITDA versus 12-16x paid in private transactions - the model does not credit a re-rating
Concentrated resort-market event risk (Maui wildfire 2023, Florida hurricanes 2024, Hawaii Kona Low 2026) and rising coastal insurance costs
Capital deployment of the ~$1.3B pro-forma cash is treated as value-neutral; acquisitions at 13x EBITDA versus buybacks at ~11.7x would change that
Third-party operator (Marriott, Hyatt) execution on labour cost is outside Host's control

inputs.cash_note: Reported cash $1,953M at 30-Jun-2026 less the $630M Q2 regular ($0.20) + special ($0.72) dividend paid 15-Jul-2026 (record date 30-Jun, accrued in payables at the balance-sheet date; the current price is ex-dividend). The $156M FF&E replacement escrow is excluded from cash because it funds the R&R capex already charged in the flows.
inputs.total_debt_note: Balance sheet 30-Jun-2026: senior notes 3,990 + credit facility incl. $999 term loans 998 + mortgage/other 94 = 5,082. The Metrics CSV TotalDebt (1,274 at FY2025) is the XBRL LongTermDebt subset tag, not total debt (DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations 5,077 at FY2025). Weighted average maturity 4.7y, weighted average rate 4.8%, no 2026 maturities.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: Unlevered pre-SBC owner FCF FY2025 = consolidated EBITDA 1,650 (operating profit 855 + D&A 795) - cash taxes 11.4 - total capex 724 (R&R + ROI, XBRL PaymentsForCapitalImprovements 282 + RealEstateImprovements 442). Company-basis levered FCF (OCF 1,510 - capex 724) = 786; the gap is interest paid 241 net of interest income and working-capital timing.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest income sits below operating profit in Host's P&L, so the EBITDA the flows are built from (operating profit + D&A) already excludes it; nothing to strip. Cash is netted against debt in the bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back $26M; the Adjusted EBITDAre and Adjusted FFO reconciliations use the same $26M (FY2026 forecast schedule, 5-Aug-2026 release). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed; SBC is 0.4% of revenue so the house/street band is negligible.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $205M; H1-2026 $75M. Host is a repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded, not a modelling convention. Shares fell 704.0M (FY2024 diluted) to 688.6M (FY2026 guidance basis).
inputs.share_count_basis: 688.6M = FY2026 diluted weighted-average share count from the 5-Aug-2026 guidance reconciliation (685.0M common at 30-Jun-2026, 685.1M on the 5-Aug-2026 10-Q cover, plus dilutive RSU/PSU). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed. Host LP OP units held by third parties are charged in the equity bridge at their 30-Jun-2026 redemption value ($226M) rather than added to the count.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Cost of equity 10.2% = 10y UST ~4.2% + beta 1.2 (lodging REIT; full hotel P&L exposure, operating leverage) x ERP 5.0%. Cost of debt 5.0% (4.8% weighted average on the stack, ~5.5% marginal on new unsecured notes); no tax shield because a REIT pays no entity-level tax. Weights at market: equity ~15.6B (22.66 x 688.6M) / debt 5.1B = 75/25. WACC = 0.75 x 10.2 + 0.25 x 5.0 = 8.9%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios - risk is charged once, through the probability weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating (ground) leases: US GAAP expenses the lease cost inside hotel operating costs, so it is already inside EBITDA (treatment A: cost in the flows). Lease liabilities ($563M) are therefore NOT added to net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is omitted (zero) to avoid charging the rent twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Redeemable non-controlling interests (Host LP OP units, $226M at 30-Jun-2026 fair value) and non-redeemable NCI ($4M) are deducted in the equity bridge. Flows are consolidated, so this charges the NCI exactly once. Unconsolidated JV interests (7 domestic JVs) are excluded from the flows (equity in earnings sits below operating profit) and added back at book ($299M, advances to and investments in affiliates) - the matching-asset rule.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (unlevered, WACC, net debt deducted), NOT the AFFO-at-cost-of-equity route. Reasons: (1) the SKILL's REIT row is for IAS-40 fair-value, externally-managed property trusts where net income is revaluation noise and the FCF inputs do not exist; Host is a US GAAP historical-cost, self-managed hotel owner whose revenue is the full hotel P&L, with real EBITDA (27%), real capex (~10-12% of revenue) and real net debt on its own balance sheet. (2) Host's Adjusted FFO ($2.15-2.18/share guided) is PRE-capex (NAREIT FFO + SBC); capitalising it at cost of equity would ignore ~$550-630M/yr of R&R and brand-mandated ROI capex, the largest cash claim after interest. A FAD-at-CoE build (AFFO ~1,489 - capex ~590 = FAD ~900, $1.31/share; at CoE 10.2% and g 2.5% = $17.4/share) is the equivalent post-interest model and lands within a dollar of this DCF's base case, which is the cross-check. (3) The sector's own valuation currency is EV/EBITDA, which is exactly what an unlevered DCF implies. REIT ADAPTATIONS: all capex (R&R + ROI) is charged - ROI projects are competitive/brand-mandated renovations, so their return is allowed only through the revenue growth path; cash tax stays at the TRS level (2.5% -> 5% of EBIT) permanently because REIT status is structural, not a shelter to un-perpetuate; net debt is pro forma for the 15-Jul-2026 dividend. CYCLICALITY: lodging is the most cyclical REIT subsector (Host EBITDA margin 27% in FY2007 -> 18% in FY2009; FY2020 EBITDA negative). FY2025/FY2026 are late-cycle, guidance-boosted years (World Cup ~70bps, Maui base-effect recovery, condo sales $16-20M, BI proceeds $7M), so the base case holds margins flat rather than extrapolating the FY2026 +100bps, and the bear case is an explicit 2027-28 downturn. UNMODELLED: $114M notes receivable and the remaining Four Seasons Orlando condo inventory are left out of the bridge (small upside); no acquisitions are assumed, consistent with guidance.
inputs.guidance_fy2026: 5-Aug-2026 (raised): comparable hotel RevPAR +4.75% to +5.25%; total revenues $6,124-6,153M (+0.2% to +0.6%, dispositions offset RevPAR); GAAP operating profit margin 14.9-15.1% (+90-110bps); comparable hotel EBITDA margin 29.6-29.7% (+40-50bps); Adjusted EBITDAre $1,820-1,840M; net income $944-962M incl. $241M gain on dispositions; D&A $753M; interest expense $241M; income taxes $52-54M; Adjusted FFO $2.15-2.18/share on 688.6M diluted shares; capex $550-630M (ROI 250-285, R&R 275-315, storm reconstruction 25-30); no further dispositions or acquisitions assumed.

bear.rationale: Bottom of FY2026 guidance, then a 2027-28 lodging downturn: revenue -8% and -4% with EBITDA margin compressing to 22% through operating leverage (calibrated to FY2007-09, when Host's revenue fell 21% and margin fell from 27% to 18%; this bear is roughly half that severity). Capex is deferred but brand standards limit the cut. Recovery FY2029-31 back to 26% margin - 100bps below today, reflecting structurally higher labour and insurance costs in coastal/wildfire markets. Terminal growth 2.0%.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +0.4% = guidance midpoint $6,138M (RevPAR +5% offset by six hotels sold in 2025-26). FY2027-30 +3.0%: RevPAR ~2.5-3% (rate-led, limited luxury supply) plus ROI-renovation ramp (Hyatt program 90% done, Marriott 37%), less the lapping of the 2026 World Cup (~70bps) and Maui base effect. Fades to 2.5% terminal. No acquisitions, per guidance.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 27.3% = guided GAAP operating margin 15.0% + D&A 753/6,138 (12.3%); includes ~0.4pp of non-recurring condo sales ($16-20M) and BI proceeds ($7M). FY2027 27.1% lets those roll off; held ~27% thereafter - rate growth offsets wage inflation, no further expansion credited (FY2019 was 27.0%, FY2025 27.0%).
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 9.6% = guidance midpoint $590M. 10.0% FY2027-29 while the Marriott transformational program runs, 9.5% thereafter (R&R ~5.5% + ROI ~4%). Below the FY2022-25 average of 12% because that period carried the Hyatt program peak and two hurricane rebuilds; above the R&R-only level because brand renovations are not optional for luxury flags.
base.tax_rationale: REIT: only TRS income is taxed. Cash taxes paid were $11-12M/yr FY2023-25 (~1.3% of EBIT); GAAP provision guided $52-54M for FY2026 (~5.5% incl. $5M on dispositions). Path 2.5% -> 5% of EBIT is between the two. Held permanently - REIT status is structural, not a carryforward to ramp to 21%.
base.da_rationale: FY2026 12.3% = guided $753M. Drifts to 11% as capex (~10%) runs below D&A and older acquired basis rolls off. Only affects the flows via the ~3-5% cash tax rate.

bull.rationale: Top of FY2026 guidance, then the expansion extends: luxury/upper-upscale RevPAR compounds 4-5% on rate with group pace strong and no new supply, renovated Hyatt/Marriott assets earn their RevPAR premium, and margins expand ~120bps to 28.5% as rate outruns wages. Capex normalises toward 9% once both transformational programs finish. Terminal growth 3.0%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: lodging is the most cyclical REIT subsector, the expansion is six years old, and FY2026 guidance embeds transitory tailwinds (World Cup, Maui base effect, condo sales) that make 2027 comparisons hard. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs sustained 4-5% rate growth AND margin expansion against wage inflation AND a multiple re-rating, three independent things. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
